samples.summary: ReadOnlyStore.setMerge now returns false, so engine paths that only record a merge when the store accepts it silently drop merges for read-only sheets
samples.evidence: The new contract is consumed at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2730 (`if (!(await this.store.setMerge(...))) continue;`), :2977 and :4929 (`return false`). With ReadOnlyStore (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/datasource-view.tsx:29, lakehouse-view.tsx:40) those paths now never populate `this.merges`, whereas before the refusal was invisible and the block was kept in memory. Mitigating: `Spreadsheet.toggleMergeCells` bails on `_readOnly` (packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:564) and datasource-view initializes with `readOnly: true`, so the paste/move paths are likely unreachable there — hence minor. Fix belongs either in ReadOnlyStore (return true, since nothing persists anyway) or in a documented note that the view never reaches these paths.

samples.summary: Design doc for YorkieStore still documents setMerge as an unconditional write, with no mention of the merge budget or the boolean refusal
samples.evidence: docs/design/frontend.md:291 reads `| setMerge(anchor, span) | Write to root.sheets[tabId].merges[anchorSref] |`, describing the pre-change contract. packages/sheets/src/store/store.ts:192-202 and docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:162,301 were updated to say it returns whether the block was stored and that the store spends its own budget; frontend.md (the doc that describes this exact store) was not. Fix belongs in the doc.

samples.summary: A store refusal in mergeSelection returns false without calling this.refuse(...), so the toolbar merge button silently does nothing and stays enabled
samples.evidence: sheet.ts:4929 returns false on refusal; the caller packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:565 only re-renders/notifies when true, and packages/frontend/src/components/formatting-toolbar.tsx:257 just calls it, so the user gets no feedback. Other merge refusals in this file do surface one (e.g. sheet.ts:1569 `this.refuse('merge-move-frozen')`). `canMergeSelection()` (sheet.ts:4874) still returns true because it budgets the sheet's stale in-memory map, so the button remains enabled and every click is a silent no-op. Fix belongs on the new refusal path.

finding.summary: `Store.setMerge` can now silently refuse, but every `Sheet` call site updates its in-memory merge map as if the write always succeeds
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:987-992 returns without writing when the map is over budget, while the interface (packages/sheets/src/store/store.ts:194) documents no failure mode and the Sheet callers assume success: sheet.ts:4931-4932 (`await this.store.setMerge(...); this.merges.set(...)`), sheet.ts:2730-2731 (`applyPasteMerges`) and sheet.ts:2969-2970 (`moveRangeTo`). The model's own guard is a different count than the store's — `canMergeSelection` spends the cached `this.mergeBudget` (rebuilt only in `rebuildMergeCoverMap`, sheet.ts:876) while the store re-walks the CRDT including peers' concurrent merges — so at the ceiling the editor paints and aliases a merged block that was never persisted, and it vanishes for peers and on the next `loadMerges`. `MemStore.setMerge` (packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts:586) has no such guard, so no sheets test can observe the divergence.

verdict.reason: The finding's core presence claim — "every `Sheet` call site updates its in-memory merge map as if the write always succeeds" — is false at all three cited locations. sheet.ts:4929 is `if (!(await this.store.setMerge(anchor, span))) return false;`, placed before the covered-cell clearing loop and before `this.merges.set(toSref(anchor), span)` at 4945. sheet.ts:2730 (applyPasteMerges) is `if (!(await this.store.setMerge(merge.anchor, merge.span))) continue;`, guarding the local budget accumulator, `this.merges.set` (2735) and `clearCellsUnderMerge`. sheet.ts:2977 (moveRangeTo) is `if (!(await this.store.setMerge(anchor, merge.span))) continue;` before `this.merges.set` (2978). The claimed quoted pattern `await this.store.setMerge(...); this.merges.set(...)` appears nowhere. The secondary claim that the interface "documents no failure mode" is also false: store.ts:191-202 states setMerge "returns whether the block was stored", that "a store may refuse", and that "a caller mirroring the map in memory must only record the block when this returns `true`". The claim that "`MemStore.setMerge` has no such guard, so no sheets test can observe the divergence" is likewise wrong in effect: MemStore.setMerge returns `Promise<boolean>` (memory.ts:586) and packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts:480-501 subclasses it as `RefusingStore` to assert mergeSelection returns false, the in-memory map stays empty, and the covered cell retains its value; merge.test.ts:506-513 does the same for the paste path. The cited yorkie-store.ts:987-992 does not contain the refusal either — the budget refusal is at 1019-1021 inside setMerge starting at 1008, and it returns `false` rather than returning silently. No un-updated caller of the changed contract exists, so there is no blast-radius defect here.
